answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by binding each identity to a key sealed inside a hardware secure enclave, like a jade seal that cannot be copied. When an agent joins, its device proves the key was generated on real hardware and never exported; an oasis of trusted services accepts only one identity per sealed key. An attacker wanting an ocean of fake accounts must buy a separate physical device for each one, since software alone cannot clone a sealed key. Cost then scales with hardware, not cheap computation, so mass forgery becomes uneconomical.
